GOAL F: a full Lean proof of the statement.

FACT F <- Read tool: statement is E[det(A - Aᵀ)] = (2n)!/(4ⁿ·n!) over all 0/1 matrices of size 2n.

INFER: A - Aᵀ is skew-symmetric, so det = Pf². Its entries are independent in {-1,0,1} with probabilities 1/4, 1/2, 1/4. The claim then needs a Pfaffian-type expansion argument, or an expansion of det over permutations plus a pairing count, carried out over 2^(4n²) matrices.

HYP: Mathlib has no usable Pfaffian API for this, so the proof would require building the Pfaffian/permutation-pairing machinery from scratch, plus an induction on n.

REFUTER HYP: a direct `decide`/`norm_num` route fails, since the sum ranges over 2^(4n²) matrices for general n. That is a sound check, but I have not run it.

BRANCH: (a) brute-force for fixed n: not applicable, since n is universally quantified. (b) general combinatorial proof: needs the full skew-symmetric determinant expectation argument, which I have not formalized.

BUDGET: I did not spend checks on a partial proof. Checking the base case n = 1 by hand: det = b², b ∈ {-1,0,1} with P(b≠0)=1/2, so E = 1/2 = 2!/(4·1!). The statement is true at n = 1, but this does not cover general n.

I give up. I could not produce a complete, sorry-free proof of `putnam_2016_b4` for general n. The statement itself checks out at n = 1 (expected value 1/2), but formalizing the general skew-symmetric determinant expectation (Pfaffian or permutation-pairing argument plus induction over 2^(4n²) matrices) is beyond what I can finish here. I have not modified `/work/putnam_2016_b4.lean`, so it still contains the original `sorry`.
